lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's BOCC meeting, where two Land Use Code amendments go before the commissioners — one updating rules for natural medicine businesses, the other reshaping what's possible on nonconforming lots, the kind of quiet code language that has real consequences for property owners across the county. That same day, HARC takes up the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave, three preliminary large-scale public hearings covering multiple new buildings in an Accommodations 2 zone. Rico's Board of Trustees also meets Tuesday to act on a water line replacement contract and a historical society lease.
